caption: I guessed R400 for garage food after night shift. It was R850. What's the number your schedule makes you spend without noticing?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R16 800
p/m salary
Living in Tzaneen
slides.body:
Female, 25
Single, shares a flat
Job: Paramedic, EMS
Net salary: R16 800 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Half of a 2 bed, water, wifi
slides.body: Shift work means I want a flatmate who's asleep when I need quiet. It's ten minutes from the station.

slides.title: Petrol & vehicle costs
slides.includes: Fuel for 24 hour shifts, tyres, basic service
slides.body: The ambulance runs on the department's fuel. My own car runs on mine, and the callout radius is bigger than people think.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Shoprite, the vending machine at the base
slides.body: I meal prep on my days off. On shift days it's whatever's fastest.

slides.title: Takeaways & garage food
slides.includes: Garage pies after night shift, the base vending machine, Friday KFC
slides.body: I guessed R400. It was R850. Night shift makes you buy things.

slides.title: Family support
slides.includes: My mom's electricity, airtime for my gran
slides.body: It goes off two days after payday. I've never once thought of it as optional.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, phone & data, medical aid top-up, funeral policy, stokvel, kit & uniform top-ups, savings
slides.body: Seven small debit orders I've never added up in one sitting. Together they're most of what's left.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R16 800. That's about R23 a day until payday, and shift work doesn't leave much room to notice when it runs out.

slides.title: I stopped guessing where it went
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The garage food number was the one I didn't see coming.

No bank login needed.
